Ford Motor Company. Ford disagrees with the implication in the NPRM that a 50-pound weight reduction is easily achievable for 1979 and that a significant fuel economy gain (1.7 percent) would result. A 50-pound weight reduction would result in only 3 percent of Ford NPA's dropping to the next lower inertia weight class. Ford claims that their NPAs are not evenly distributed in their respective inertia weight classes. Therefore, a 50-pound weight reduction would achieve only a 0.08 percent fuel economy increase for Ford, in contrast to the 1.7 percent implied in the NPRM.
General Motors Corporation (GM). GM agrees with the NHTSA analysis that a 50-pound weight reduction in all vehicles would shift nearly 10 percent of the vehicles to the next lower inertia weight class. However, GM disagrees with the NHTSA estimate that an average 50-pound weight reduction will result in a 1.7 percent improvement of average fuel economy.
